answer: The most convincing defense is on-ledger slashing of verifiers: every transaction countersignature is a bonded stake, and if a verifier signs an invalid state transition, the delta between honest and fraudulent behavior is seized from that bond — priced strictly above the maximum epoch reward, so a single bad signature erases months of income. Because each fake identity must post the same unforgeable bond up front, a sybil spiral becomes uneconomic: every additional account multiplies capital at risk while verification stays probabilistic, like a vault
